result.rationale: The diff shows prisma.booking.update with attendees createMany committed before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking), which has no try/catch (unlike sendAddGuestsEmails, which is wrapped). If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the mutation errors after attendees are persisted. A retry then hits the filter `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, yielding uniqueGuests.length === 0 and throwing BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' — a misleading error despite the guests already being added. Both mechanisms are directly verifiable in addGuests.handler.ts.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation updates the DB first via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...) and only afterwards calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) with no transaction/rollback or try/catch. If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the request errors after guests are already persisted. On retry, uniqueGuests is computed by filtering out emails already present in booking.attendees, so uniqueGuests can become empty and the handler throws BAD_REQUEST with message "emails_must_be_unique_valid", matching the described misleading failure mode.
